source.author: stat
source.text: Ipsum etiam proprio certamina festa labore dignari et tumulo supremum hunc addere honorem hortantur proceres ac, ne victoria desit una ducum numero, fundat vel Lyctia cornu tela rogant, tenui vel nubila transeat hasta, obsequitur gaudens, viridique ex aggere in aecum stipatus summis iuvenum descendit; at illi pone leves portat pharetras et cornua iussus armiger: ingentem iactu transmittere circum eminus et dictae dare vulnera destinat orno.
source.text_original: Ipsum etiam proprio certamina festa labore / dignari et tumulo supremum hunc addere honorem / hortantur proceres ac, ne victoria desit / una ducum numero, fundat vel Lyctia cornu / tela rogant, tenui vel nubila transeat hasta, / obsequitur gaudens, viridique ex aggere in aecum / stipatus summis iuvenum descendit; at illi / pone leves portat pharetras et cornua iussus / armiger: ingentem iactu transmittere circum / eminus et dictae dare vulnera destinat orno.
source.text_english: They also urge him to deem the festival combats worthy of his own labor and to add this final honor to the tomb; and they beg that, lest one victory be missing from the tally of the leaders, he should hurl his weapons even from the Lyctian bow, or pass the cloudy shaft through the thin air. He complies gladly, and, packed with the foremost youths, descends from the green embankment into the plain; but behind him the armour-bearer carries the light quivers and horns, as ordered. He intends, by a cast from afar, to send the huge spear around the circuit and to inflict the promised wounds with the ash-wood shaft.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: fluctibus e mediis terras dabit ille magistro et dabit astra rati, cumque aethera Iuppiter umbra perdiderit, solus transibit nubila Lynceus.
reuse.text_original: fluctibus e mediis terras dabit ille magistro / et dabit astra rati, cumque aethera Iuppiter umbra / perdiderit, solus transibit nubila Lynceus.
reuse.text_english: He will give lands from the midst of the waves to the helmsman, and he will give the stars to the ship, and when Jupiter has lost the sky in shadow, Lynceus alone will pass through the clouds.
